// Part: room: gazebo. Interior of the octagonal pavilion (box x10..16, y2..6, z78..84), furnished by the interior designer.
// Layout: a round table on a dark-oak fence post at the centre (13,81) with a slab top and a flower pot on it; a ring of
// stair seats facing it (north and south seats at z79/z83, east and west seats at x11/x15); flower pots in the four
// corners; five hanging lanterns (four corners and the centre) under the solid cone ceiling at y7.
// The entrance lane runs down x13 from the north opening (13,2,77) to the table; (13,79) and (13,80) stay clear.
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  const legend = {
    F: "flower_pot", // corner pots on the floor (y2)
    P: "flower_pot", // the table's pot (y4, on the slab top)
    n: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "north", half: "bottom" }], // seat on the north side, back to the north
    s: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "south", half: "bottom" }], // seat on the south side, back to the south
    w: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "west", half: "bottom" }], // seat on the west side, back to the west
    e: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "east", half: "bottom" }], // seat on the east side, back to the east
    T: "dark_oak_fence", // table post (y2)
    t: ["dark_oak_slab", { type: "top" }], // table top (y3, top half)
    L: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }], // hanging lanterns (y6), from the cone's solid ceiling at y7
  };
  // x10..16 across, z78..84 down; the outer ring is the pavilion's balustrade and columns, left alone.
  const blank = ["       ", "       ", "       ", "       ", "       ", "       ", "       "];
  const y2 = [
    "       ", // z78
    " Fn nF ", // z79
    " w   e ", // z80
    " w T e ", // z81
    " w   e ", // z82
    " Fs sF ", // z83
    "       ", // z84
  ];
  const y3 = ["       ", "       ", "       ", "   t   ", "       ", "       ", "       "];
  const y4 = ["       ", "       ", "       ", "   P   ", "       ", "       ", "       "];
  // corner lanterns sit one cell in from the octagon corners (those cells hold the earlier part's balustrade)
  const y6 = ["       ", "       ", "  L L  ", "   L   ", "  L L  ", "       ", "       "];
  // layers from y2: [floor furniture, table top, table pot, (y5 air), hanging lanterns]
  layers(g, [10, 2, 78], legend, [y2, y3, y4, blank, y6]);
}

input.summary:
Gazebo needs no extra light: in the designed geometry (scratch build with h4 SITE_Y=0) it is 28/28 reachable, min light 9, 0 dark, 0 dim, from the 5 existing hanging lanterns. parts/room-36.mjs is unchanged; I added no lamps.
The shipped build.nbt still reads 7 dim cells and "NEEDS WORK" because vocab/h4.mjs writes the gazebo 4 blocks high (floor at y5 not y1, roof at y11 not y7). That is a kit bug, not fixed here, and lamps added to cover it would have to be removed after the fix.
Scratch copy at /tmp/lamp-43-scratch (h4 SITE_Y set to 0 in the copy only); crew files untouched apart from make.sh's build.nbt.
left: vocab/h4.mjs line 13 `SITE_Y = 4` plus put()'s `y + SITE_Y` (line 40) is a stale site-to-grid offset: the grid is plan y 0..32 now (base.mjs). Every h4 helper (gazebo, ventArch, chimneyStack, rearPorch, magnolia, gatePier, riverBand) lands 4 blocks high in build.nbt. Fix: SITE_Y = 0 and update vocab/test-h4.mjs (it assumes 4). After the fix, the gazebo room should pass with no change from me: 28/28 reachable, min 9, 0 dark, 0 dim (verified in the scratch build).

Gazebo eave ring (grounds/h4 gazebo): 20 FIT issues 'deepslate_tile_stairs stands on a bottom slab'. The octEdge(4) smooth_quartz slab at y+5 is bottom-type and the first roof course sits on it at y+6, leaving half a block of air. Fix in h4 gazebo: make that slab type top, or drop the first course by a half. Owner: grounds / h4.
build.nbt as shipped: `mcd room --only gazebo` exits 1 (walk UNREACHABLE 0 of 31, 7 dim cells, floating pots and lanterns). All of it follows from the h4 offset; none of it is a lamp problem.

waste.what: Worked out the gazebo's real y by hand: dumped slices with a throwaway script (first attempt used the wrong Grid accessor) to find that the shell sits at y5, not y1.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and 2 script retries

waste.what: `mcd room` samples light at the floor row it infers (y=3 here, under the broken floor). I had to rerun `mcd light --y 6` to measure the real stands.
waste.tool: `mcd room` should take `--feet-y` or infer the floor from the room box's y0, and report which row it sampled.

structured_output.summary:
Gazebo needs no extra light: in the designed geometry (scratch build with h4 SITE_Y=0) it is 28/28 reachable, min light 9, 0 dark, 0 dim, from the 5 existing hanging lanterns. parts/room-36.mjs is unchanged; I added no lamps.
The shipped build.nbt still reads 7 dim cells and "NEEDS WORK" because vocab/h4.mjs writes the gazebo 4 blocks high (floor at y5 not y1, roof at y11 not y7). That is a kit bug, not fixed here, and lamps added to cover it would have to be removed after the fix.
Scratch copy at /tmp/lamp-43-scratch (h4 SITE_Y set to 0 in the copy only); crew files untouched apart from make.sh's build.nbt.
left: vocab/h4.mjs line 13 `SITE_Y = 4` plus put()'s `y + SITE_Y` (line 40) is a stale site-to-grid offset: the grid is plan y 0..32 now (base.mjs). Every h4 helper (gazebo, ventArch, chimneyStack, rearPorch, magnolia, gatePier, riverBand) lands 4 blocks high in build.nbt. Fix: SITE_Y = 0 and update vocab/test-h4.mjs (it assumes 4). After the fix, the gazebo room should pass with no change from me: 28/28 reachable, min 9, 0 dark, 0 dim (verified in the scratch build).

Gazebo eave ring (grounds/h4 gazebo): 20 FIT issues 'deepslate_tile_stairs stands on a bottom slab'. The octEdge(4) smooth_quartz slab at y+5 is bottom-type and the first roof course sits on it at y+6, leaving half a block of air. Fix in h4 gazebo: make that slab type top, or drop the first course by a half. Owner: grounds / h4.
build.nbt as shipped: `mcd room --only gazebo` exits 1 (walk UNREACHABLE 0 of 31, 7 dim cells, floating pots and lanterns). All of it follows from the h4 offset; none of it is a lamp problem.
